data.name: Dwarakaa
data.gender_notes: Dwarakaa is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Dwarakaa is a name of the goddess Lakshmi, the goddess of wealth, fortune, and prosperity in Hindu mythology. She is the consort of Lord Vishnu and is particularly revered in the city of Dwarka. Dwarakaa is believed to bestow her blessings upon her devotees, bringing them wealth, happiness, and prosperity. The name Dwarakaa carries the meaning “Goddess of Dwarka” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Dwarakaa usually hope their child will grow to embody goddess of dwarka and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Dwarakaa belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Goddess of Dwarka.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Dwarakaa total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

historical_references.reference: According to Hindu mythology, Dwarka is the name of a legendary city in India, believed to be the capital of the Yadava dynasty, where Lord Krishna resided towards the end of his earthly life.

The name Dwarka is mentioned in the ancient Indian texts, Rigveda and Mahabharata, as the name of a city believed to have been founded by the god, Vishnu, and later served as the capital city of the Yadavas under the rule of Krishna.
